content:
Priya M.: Quick RFC follow-up on hybrid fallback for canary/A-B. I sketched a local-first coordinator + optional central arbitrator. Goal: keep tail-latency tiny while preserving global safety and observability.
Alex B.: what immediate problems are we solving with the hybrid?
Priya M.: model quality regressions, node OOMs/capacity loss, region partitions, and slow/absent control-plane telemetry.
Samir K.: if local acts independently for too long we risk drift. How long before central overrides?
Priya M.: plan: local makes instant, deterministic decisions for immediate safety (response < 5ms extra). It logs compact actions to central. Central reevaluates larger windows and can issue higher-precedence directives.
Elena R.: local policy shape? simple thresholds? state machine?
Priya M.: tiny state machine. Triggers: consecutive error windows, p95 exceed, oom events, or QPS saturation. Fallbacks only to compatible variants; local uses cached compatibility blob.
Marco L.: how to keep the compatibility blob current without querying central on every check?
Priya M.: config sync pushes a small compatibility blob to nodes; refresh TTL ~ 5m by default. Local decisions consult blob, not central discovery.
Alex B.: private/VPC customers: central may be unreachable. Local autonomy must fully work standalone, right?
Priya M.: yes. In air-gapped installs, local runs in autonomous-only mode and persists action logs locally. On reconnect, it ships logs for reconciliation.
Samir K.: reconciliation semantics? We need ordering and idempotency. Sequence numbers per-node? LWW? CRDT?
Priya M.: proposal: per-node monotonic seq numbers plus central generation counters. Central accepts action logs and applies LWW with seq+generation checks, then recomputes canonical state.
Elena R.: add safety: cooldown windows and exponential backoff to prevent flip-flopping. Local policy must include cooldown.
Priya M.: yes. Default cooldown 2 minutes, backoff x2 with jitter.
Alex B.: telemetry budget: what exactly do nodes send to central? can't flood control plane.
Priya M.: compact payloads: small rolling aggregates (p50,p95,error_rate,qps) per window, and action-events list. Sampled traces at low rate (eg 1/1000). We downsample aggressively at source.
Marco L.: runbooks for disagreement: if central and node disagree > T (10m), page oncall and optionally force central directive.
Priya M.: propose automatic escalation: after 10m divergent, send alert and if configured, central can flip a forced directive (configurable per-deployment).
Samir K.: edge case: replay storms when node reconnects and pushes long backlog. Need replay-rate-limits and dedupe by seq.
Priya M.: agreed. central will enforce ingestion rate limits, ack ranges, and ignore duplicates by node+seq.
Alex B.: sample local policy JSON snippet?
Priya M.: snippet below (as text):
{
  "policy_version": "1",
  "triggers": {
    "error_rate": {"threshold": "0.03", "consecutive_windows": "3"},
    "p95_ms": {"threshold": "350", "consecutive_windows": "2"},
    "oom_event": {"threshold": "1"}
  },
  "fallback": "switch_to_compatible_variant",
  "cooldown_s": "120",
  "backoff_multiplier": "2"
}
Alex B.: how does local undo happen if central later decides no rollback?
Priya M.: central directives include a generation number. Nodes honor central directives with higher generation; local-originated actions include node seq so central can reference them. Central can issue an explicit undo or a new pin.
Elena R.: prioritize origins: capacity-safety (node emergency) > central-pin > central-suggestion > local-autonomy. That helps deterministic conflict resolution.
Marco L.: cost/observability: add a cost-impact metric to action events so finance can see churn.
Priya M.: added. action-events include optional cost_delta field.
Samir K.: I'll draft the reconciliation algorithm: sequence-based LWW + central re-eval and convergence step. Will include anti-entropy checks.
Alex B.: I'll sketch a minimal control-plane directive API: POST /v1/directives {target, generation, action, reason}. Simple auth for now.
Priya M.: thanks. Open questions for thread: 1) action-log schema compact vs verbose, 2) reconciliation: LWW vs merge, 3) sane default thresholds and cooldowns.
Elena R.: vote: compact log + LWW with seq nums. Easier to audit.
Marco L.: add config flag for private-only mode to disable central expectations.
Samir K.: will include replay rate limits, dedupe, and ordering guarantees in the RFC blurb.
deploy-bot: "deployment: canary-hybrid 0.2.0 -> staging succeeded" :white_check_mark:
Priya M.: thanks all, I'll update the RFC with this hybrid flow, include the policy snippet, runbook and example alerts, and open a PR tomorrow. Tagging @Alex B., @Samir K., @Elena R. for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
